release_notes: Security release for the October 2026 PHP vulnerabilities. CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 ("php2shell") are unauthenticated remote-code-execution bugs in PHP itself with a public exploit; every web-facing PHP server is exposed, and a tracker is web-facing by definition — Orbitra's own code is not the attack surface, the interpreter is. Fix the server packages: patched PHP releases are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 (run "apt update && apt upgrade 'php*'" and restart php-fpm and nginx). On PHP 8.1 or older no fix will ever come — the branch is end-of-life; re-run "sudo bash install.sh" and it installs PHP 8.5 alongside the old one and switches nginx and FPM over. Distro builds may carry the fix backported under the old version number (check: apt changelog php-fpm | grep 109618); if PHP was installed by a hosting panel (ispmanager and the like), update it from that panel. After this panel update a red dashboard banner judges your server's PHP and shows the exact commands until it reports a fixed version; the in-panel updater prints the same advisory, and docs/deployment.md (Updating PHP) spells out both paths.
